key_insight: Iterative refinement—a repeated propose-verify-correct loop at inference—substantially improves text-to-image alignment on complex, compositional prompts by enforcing multiple objects, relations, and attributes stepwise.
problem_solved: Text-to-image models struggle to satisfy many simultaneous constraints in richly compositional prompts; standard fixes (more denoising steps or parallel sampling) are insufficient to reliably produce correct multi-object/relational scenes.
method: Run generation as an iterative loop: propose an image (or latent), verify which prompt constraints are unmet, and apply targeted corrections.
Use a lightweight verifier/feedback signal (e.g., captioning/scoring or constraint-checker) to detect mismatches and guide subsequent refinement steps.
Apply corrections across denoising/latent steps so constraints are enforced progressively rather than only at final sampling.
impact: Enables practitioners to produce more reliable, constraint-satisfying images from existing T2I models without retraining, improving utility for complex scene generation, dataset creation, and downstream evaluation tasks.
visual_elements: Flowchart of the iterative propose → verify → correct loop (annotated with where verifier feedback is injected).
Before/after image pairs for a complex prompt showing error modes fixed by refinement (e.g., swapped objects, missing attributes).
Bar/line chart comparing prompt-constraint satisfaction rates vs. baseline methods (single-pass, extra denoising, parallel sampling).
Schematic illustrating verifier types (captioning, classifier, symbolic constraint checker) feeding corrective updates into the sampler.
paper_title: Iterative Refinement Improves Compositional Image Generation
paper_authors: Shantanu Jaiswal, Mihir Prabhudesai, Nikash Bhardwaj, Zheyang Qin, Amir Zadeh
